correctness.rationale: Sixteen divisors of squarefree four-prime n form eight complementary pairs. Removing omitted pairs must sum Δ=σ(n)−2n; nonnegative Δ forces even n, then elementary abundancy bounds reduce the three smallest primes to a small family, with sole exceptional 2·7·11·13 ruled out by any pair sum exceeding Δ=28. For n=6bc, Δ=12(b+c+1), four small complementary pairs sum only 12(b+c), forcing an omitted large pair and (b−12)(c−12)≤150, bounding b. The remaining 10 squarefree three-prime cores m admit 256 subsets each; in every case the pair omission identity (A−σ(m)+2m)c=σ(m)−B has no double-zero coefficient case. Exhaustive exact rational/integer mask enumeration gives exactly n={210,330,546,714,1770,3198,3486}, one mask each, all containing the pair (1,n) in the retained set. The unrestricted large-prime conclusion follows from the symbolic linear equation plus finite cores, not a bounded brute-force search.
